金づちを持つと、世界に釘が増える――when tools start defining the problem

“If all you have is a hammer, everything looks like a nail” is deeper than overusing a favorite tool. This essay follows Kaplan, Maslow, fixation research, chess eye-tracking, and recent AI research to ask how familiar methods reshape problem definitions and attention itself. The practical move is not merely to collect more tools, but to define the desired change before naming the tool.
